claims.claim: The unaccent extension does NOT strip Hebrew nikud (U+0591-U+05C7); its default rules cover only Latin/Greek combining marks (U+0300-U+0362). Strip Hebrew nikud with regexp_replace over the Hebrew points range in an IMMUTABLE function.
claims.raw_snippet: unaccent — a text search dictionary which removes diacritics # F.48.1. Configuration F.48.2. Usage F.48.3. Functions unaccent is a text search dictionary that removes accents (diacritic signs) from lexemes. It's a filtering dictionary, which means its output is always passed to the next dictionary (if any), unlike the normal behavior of dictionaries. This allows accent-insensitive processing for full text search.

claims.claim: A non-deterministic collation may treat strings as equal even when their bytes differ (accent-insensitive / normalization-insensitive comparison); this is what makes nikud and sofit folding possible at a reduced ICU strength.
claims.raw_snippet: Nondeterministic comparison may determine strings to be equal even if they consist of different bytes. Typical situations include case-insensitive comparison, accent-insensitive comparison, as well as comparison of strings in different Unicode normal forms.

claims.claim: Non-deterministic collations carry a performance penalty, block B-tree deduplication, and are rejected by some pattern-matching operations (PostgreSQL 17 raises "nondeterministic collations are not supported for LIKE"). They do NOT block UNIQUE constraints or plain btree indexes.
claims.raw_snippet: Foremost, their use leads to a performance penalty. Note, in particular, that B-tree cannot use deduplication with indexes that use a nondeterministic collation. Also, certain operations are not possible with nondeterministic collations, such as some pattern matching operations.

claims.claim: ICU custom collations (he-IL-x-icu, deterministic vs non-deterministic) are configured per the PostgreSQL ICU collation docs.
